doc.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: Cousin Bill Schaap and booing at Folk City
summary: With cousin Bill he saw shows, booed folk acts including Dylan, and went for blues acts like Sonny Terry.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Yeah my mother did too. I mean we went to the events. But the person who I’m leaving out from a family thing is that so my father and mother took me to these things, and I went out and then the musicians took me to some of these things. But my cousin Bill, Bill Schaap, Dick’s younger brother, he stepped into the breech and started, I piggy backed on his enthusiasms and goodness. I mean he’s a good guy. His wife stopped answering the telephone because I took him out of the house and I guess she didn’t like jazz. He took me to see everything. We even booed Dylan at Gerde’s Folk City, which wasn’t called Gerde’s yet, it was just Folk City. I think it was before they took over Tony Pastor’s joint, before they moved. And the only reason why I know it was Dylan who we booed is because he became famous so quickly after. Because they would have the new folk singer who wanted to be the next Pete Seeger I guess or Dylan would probably say Woody Guthrie. And they would be the emcee but they would do a few songs at the start of the show. And I really wasn’t into — there was this Hootenanny craze.
So we’re in the same tribe, huh Monk, yeah, yeah, yeah? You seem to know as much about the fifties and sixties.

But it was cool with me but it wasn’t cool. And so if you wanted to go to Folk City to see a blues act, because they had blues acts, like Sonny Terry, who was my neighbor. I used to hit home runs, whiffle ball into his yard. I think he lived at the corner of Keno and Pompey in Hollis. And we didn’t want to hear this unknown folk singer do his thing, so you booed him to make sure he didn’t do an encore or anything.
Oh yeah. It didn’t matter whether it was Dylan or not. Whoever it was you booed.

Let’s say this was the bill. You know, I’m not saying this was the bill, you have Joan Baez, Pete Seeger, Peter, Paul & Mary, Benny Goodman and an unknown folk singer. And so if I went to that, I went to hear Benny Goodman. Even though Peter, Paul & Mary and Joan Baez and all these others are famous people, I’ll tolerate them because they’re famous, I want to hear what they have to do, but I’m going to be sitting on my hands for three hours waiting for the Benny Goodman or whatever, Sonny Terry and Brownie

McGee which I went to see many times. That’s what I want to see. So I’m not going to encourage an encore. I’m trying to get rid of this thing. But because he became famous so fast I remembered it was him.
Sure. Well he had a pretty distinctive sound at the time too.

Yeah but that wasn’t it, it was just he was the guy and you booed him. I booed others whose names I don’t know. I know him because he became famous. Every time I went to Folk City it was to see the blues act. Never once to see the folk act. Not once. It doesn’t make them bad, it doesn’t hopefully make me bad. But I went to see the blues act. And so the new hootenanny wannabe who was the emcee got short shrift from me, and my cousin Bill, and at one time it was Dylan.
